b: The University of Texas, Dallas (UTD) earned a return trip to the Collegiate Chess League Finals by earning a first-round bye and then defeating Texas Tech in the Semifinals. They will play the winner of the upcoming semifinal match between the Saint Louis University (SLU) and the University of Missouri (Mizzou) to decide the champion of the fall 2026 season.
UTD waits for the winner of the SLU - Mizzou semifinals.

As the top two seeds, SLU and UTD earned byes in the playoffs, making it straight to the Semifinals. The lower seeds had to earn their spot in the next round. Mizzou faced the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) in the quarterfinals. Mizzou led from start to finish, taking the match 11-4. GM Gergely Kantor scored a perfect 4-0 to lead his team to victory.

The other quarterfinal match saw the first tiebreaker of the season. The SRM Institute of Science and Technology fought Texas Tech to an 8-8 tie at the end of regulation. In the regular season, that would be the end of the story, but just one team could advance to the Semifinals. NM Nathaniel Moor won a critical endgame victory to clinch an overtime victory for Texas Tech by an 11-9 final margin.

While Mizzou and SLU have yet to play, UTD punched their ticket back to the finals with a 10-6 victory over Texas Tech. GM Ido Gorshtein led the way with an undefeated 3/4 score, including this attacking victory over Moor.
You can watch the UTD vs Texas Tech broadcast, hosted by Joe Lee.
The Collegiate Chess League is the premier online chess competition for college students.
NM Jeremy Kane is the Instructional Content Manager for Chess.com, and the author of several courses in the Starting Out series, Queen’s Gambit Accepted, Trompowsky, and Tarrasch.
